title: Assassin's Quest
author: Hobb, Robin
review:
August 2025:
Still an amazing read. Knowing the full story makes me appreciate everything Hobb set up here that pays off in later books.

July 2020:
Robin Hobb makes you care about her characters so much that it hurts a little bit. The way she writes just completely transports my mind into her world; it's wonderful. Fitz gets metaphorically and sometimes literally kicked in the balls repeatedly but he endures. This entry changes up from the previous two in the titular 'quest' fashion, it's a peek from the peephole of Fitz's perspective to a larger world and is refreshing. There is a bit of bloat in this entry and could have been condensed some, but honestly it's nice to spend time with these characters even if they're doing mundane things such as setting up camp or surviving in the wilderness. I ravenously consumed this one and still want more.
